planCorrections.issue: ped-sec-14 (Colin et al.) author-name discrepancy discovered at Phase 1.
planCorrections.resolution: The article's own citation line names the corresponding/lead author's surname as 'Barrett' (Robin Colin Alexander Barrett — 'Colin' is a middle name, not the surname the plan's author-string implies). Kept id/slug/folder as Phase 0 assigned them ('colin-vr-desktop-2d', matching the plan's own §1C table so cross-references stay stable), but the unit's `citation` field uses the article's own author line and flags the discrepancy via a `citationNote`. Not a blocking issue — the plan's own short-title convention ('Colin et al.') tracks the filename, not necessarily first-author surname order.

planCorrections.issue: ped-sec-15 (Cook et al. 2011) expectedConditions guess in the plan's own Phase-1 steering note was half-wrong.
planCorrections.resolution: The steering note suggested this meta-analysis would operationalize both 'review / meta-analytic aggregate' and 'screen-based virtual patient / sim'. In fact Cook et al. explicitly excludes computer-based virtual-patient simulations from its scope (citing their own separate 2010 review of that literature). Set to 'review / meta-analytic aggregate' only; the exclusion is noted in the unit's own metadata to keep it clearly distinguished from ped-sec-19 (Kononowicz, virtual patients, which does cover that condition). No `bridgeCandidates.vle` link recorded — the meta-analysis operates at too general a level (simulation-vs-no-intervention across all health professions) to plausibly bridge to a specific vle-0N node.

planCorrections.issue: User added 11 new source PDFs to corpus/pedagogy/ after Phase 1 completed for the original 23 units, all related to 'social presence theory in education' (user's own framing, 2026-07-15).
planCorrections.resolution: Added as a new Strand F — 'Social presence theory: CMC foundations & VR-collaborative applications' (ped-sec-25..34, 9 units: the foundational CMC/online-learning social-presence tradition from Short et al.'s 1976 theory through Gunawardena & Zittle's 1997 scale, Garrison/Anderson/Archer's 1999 Community of Inquiry framework, through to Richardson et al.'s 2017 meta-analysis, plus two VR-specific bridge pieces — De Back/Tinga/Louwerse 2021 and VanderMeer et al. 2023 — connecting this CMC tradition to the VR/immersive literature already in the cluster). This strand directly grounds the 'social presence / co-presence' construct-axis row, which has been in the plan's §3 frozen vocabulary since G0 but had no dedicated source until now (structurally identical to how the Boredom cluster's bor-sec-25/26 Elpidorou additions grounded a previously-ungrounded construct row). A 10th new source (Dalgarno & Lee 2012, an explicit followup to already-in-cluster ped-sec-04) is about task affordances, not social presence per se, and was filed as ped-sec-24 under Strand B instead, with an `extends-reading-of` edge to ped-sec-04. User confirmed 2026-07-15 (mid-session prose exchange, not a formal G0 re-vote since the underlying cluster scope/purpose is unchanged, only its source coverage — but treated with the same rigor).

planCorrections.issue: Mislabeled file discovered among the user's added sources, same failure pattern as the Boredom cluster's bor-sec-18 incident.
planCorrections.resolution: The file named 'De Back, Tycho, et al. - Learning in immersed collaborative virtual environments - design and implementation (2021).pdf' (as first supplied) was NOT that paper — pdfinfo/pdftotext confirmed its actual title page read Terry, Krista P. & Peter E. Doolittle (2019), 'Re-examining Social Presence: Implications for Digital Pedagogies,' Technology, Instruction, Cognition and Learning 11:121-139. Flagged to the user before building any unit under either name (AskUserQuestion). User's resolution: renamed the mislabeled file to its true identity (now on disk as 'Terry, Krista & Peter Doolittle - Re-examining social presence - implications for digital pedagogies (2019).pdf', built as ped-sec-31) AND supplied the genuine De Back, Tinga & Louwerse (2021) paper ('Learning in immersed collaborative virtual environments: design and implementation,' Interactive Learning Environments 31(8):5364-5382, DOI 10.1080/10494820.2021.2006238), verified via its own title page and built as ped-sec-33. No content was built under a false attribution at any point.

planCorrections.issue: ped-sec-33 (De Back, Tinga & Louwerse 2021) does not perform the CMC-to-VR social-presence bridge that Strand F's design assumed for it, discovered at Phase 1.
planCorrections.resolution: The Phase-1 agent confirmed via full-text check that this paper never uses the term 'social presence' and cites none of the CMC-tradition Strand F sources (Short et al., Gunawardena & Zittle, Garrison/Anderson/Archer, Tu, Biocca/Burgoon/Harms, Richardson et al.). Its actual interlocutors are the VR-pedagogy-framework literature already elsewhere in the cluster (Dalgarno & Lee, Fowler, Mayer, Parong & Mayer, Merchant) plus Heeter/Steuer for general spatial presence. Its real content: VLE design recommendations (cognitive load, collaborative learning, platform affordances/limitations) illustrated by a CAVE-based neuroanatomy environment (two studies, n=40 and n=158) and a novel automated behavioral-logging method. Phase 2/3 must NOT overstate this unit's role as a CMC-to-VR bridge — that connection is this cluster's own construction (P/anticipatory-application), not a claim De Back et al. make themselves. ped-sec-34 (VanderMeer 2023) is the stronger candidate for a genuine bridge role — it cites De Back, Tinga, Nguyen & Louwerse (2020, a companion paper) directly and surveys the VR-collaborative-learning literature broadly, though it too does not cite the CMC-tradition canon (Garrison, Gunawardena, Short/Williams/Christie, Walther all confirmed absent). Also flagged, non-blocking: two citation-year discrepancies in ped-sec-33's own references (Dalgarno & Lee cited as 2010 vs. this cluster's ped-sec-04 manifest year of 2009; Fowler cited as 2015 vs. ped-sec-05's manifest year of 2014) and an online-2021/print-2023 publication-date discrepancy in its own masthead.

themes: cognitive load & seductive details in IVR
social presence: theory, measurement & the CMC-to-VR bridge
debate_axes_seeds: more immersion -> more learning <-> immersion adds presence but not learning (Makransky 2019; Parong & Mayer 2018 vs affordance optimism of Dalgarno & Lee, Radianti)
media-comparison designs are informative <-> methods-not-media / value-added is the valid paradigm (Mayer et al. 2022)
presence as technology-determined (immersion-driven; Witmer & Singer) <-> presence as psychologically/individually determined (Lombard & Ditton; Chow's SEM determinants)
affective route (presence -> enjoyment/motivation -> learning; Makransky & Lilleholt, CAMIL) <-> cognitive-load route (presence -> distraction/extraneous load -> less learning; Parong & Mayer 2020)
desktop-3D is a sufficient, cost-effective proxy for IVR <-> IVR carries unique affordances (Colin et al.; Merchant; Makransky-equivalence vs CAMIL/Radianti)
simulation beats no-intervention strongly <-> sim-vs-sim differences negligible (Cook et al.; Kononowicz)
cybersickness/novelty as substantive moderator of IVR learning <-> ignorable side-effect (Cossio vs most Strand-C designs)
deployment context matters (lab vs home vs classroom) <-> context-equivalence (Makransky-equivalence; Part III's own poles)

social presence reliably predicts satisfaction/learning in CMC <-> its effects are inconsistent, confounded, or assumed-not-demonstrated (Richardson & Swan, Gunawardena & Zittle vs Kreijns et al.'s pitfalls critique; Biocca/Burgoon/Harms's measurement critique)

social presence is medium-general (a CMC-tradition construct portable to any mediated communication, including VR) <-> social presence in immersive VR is qualitatively different from text-based CMC social presence (De Back/Tinga/Louwerse, VanderMeer vs the CMC-tradition papers' own text/audio-conferencing operationalizations) — ADDED 2026-07-15 (Strand F)
